scenarios.name: US tariff on EU spirits (25%)
scenarios.description: A 25% US import tariff on EU-origin spirits, against the WTO-bound zero they normally enter at. The US is the most exposed market in the portfolio because ex-works is the largest share of its shelf price, so the tariff has less existing tax to hide behind.

scenarios.name: Bottle locally in the US instead of exporting bottled
scenarios.description: Ship bulk spirit and bottle in-market under a 25% tariff. The dutiable value falls to the spirit alone and bulk freight is cheaper, so the tariff applies to a much smaller base. A local bottling cost is added after duty, where it is not dutiable. This is the structural answer to a tariff rather than a forecast of one.

scenarios.name: China anti-dumping duty on EU brandy (34.9%)
scenarios.description: China's definitive anti-dumping duty on EU brandy, stacked on the existing 5% import tariff. It lands on a handful of cognac series that carry a disproportionate share of value, which is why the volume effect and the value effect diverge sharply.
